init_sequence: 1. uwb_hw_bringup_and_init() [uwb_bringup.c:37]:    uwb_port_init() → uwb_port_hw_reset() → uwb_port_read_dev_id() →    uwb_port_set_spi_slow() → dwt_initialise(DWT_LOADUCODE) → uwb_port_set_spi_fast(). 2. dwt_initialise(DWT_LOADUCODE) [deca_device.c:183]:    soft reset → OTP LDO tune kick → XTAL trim from OTP → load LDE microcode from ROM.    Reads SYS_CFG into local copy (preserving POR default).    Does NOT read OTP antenna delays. Does NOT write TX_POWER, TC_PGDELAY, or DIS_STXP.    DWT_LOADUCODE = 0x01 — no OTP PID/LID/BAT/TMP read flags are set. 3. ss_twr_*_configure_radio() [per-role source files]:    dwt_configure(&config) → sets channel, PRF, preamble, data rate, SFD, AGC, LDE, PLL, RF_TXCTRL.    Does NOT call dwt_configuretxrf() — TX_POWER and TC_PGDELAY remain at POR defaults.    Does NOT call dwt_setsmarttxpower() — DIS_STXP remains at POR default (0 = smart power ENABLED).    DOES call dwt_setrxantennadelay() and dwt_settxantennadelay() with 16436U. 4. tag_print_otp_diag() [tag_app.c:265] is DIAGNOSTIC ONLY (gated by APP_TAG_OTP_DIAG).    Reads OTP addresses 0x01C/0x01D/0x01E and prints values but does NOT use them for configuration.

smart_tx_power.dis_stxp_state: POR default = 0 → Smart TX Power ENABLED. Application never calls dwt_setsmarttxpower(). No code writes the DIS_STXP bit.

frame_durations_us.calculation_note: At 6.8 Mbps, preamble 128 symbols, non-standard SFD (8 symbols): preamble=127.18us + SFD=7.95us + PHR=19.49us + data=(PSDU*8/6.8)us

smart_tx_power.smart_tx_power_bucket: ALL frames < 0.25 ms → ALL use BOOSTP250 power level
smart_tx_power.analysis: With Smart TX Power enabled (DIS_STXP=0, POR default), the DW1000 selects TX power based on frame duration thresholds. At 6.8 Mbps with 128-symbol preamble, ALL BioSpur frames (17B poll, 36B V3 response, 20B V1 response, 13B anchor-init poll) have total durations between 170-197 µs, which ALL fall in the BOOSTP250 bucket (< 0.25 ms). Therefore Smart TX Power introduces ZERO power differential between poll and response frames. The power asymmetry concern is MOOT for this configuration. NOTE: The POR default TX_POWER value 0x0E082848 (Ch5 PRF64) has BOOSTP250=0x08 for all these frames. If TX power were configured manually via dwt_configuretxrf(), the DW1000 User Manual Table 18 recommends 0x0E082848 for Ch5 PRF64 smart mode, or 0x1F1F1F1F for manual mode. Neither is called.

antenna_delay.tx_antd_source: Hardcoded #define per role: SS_TWR_INIT_TX_ANT_DLY=16436U, SS_TWR_RESP_TX_ANT_DLY=16436U, SS_TWR_ANCHOR_INIT_TX_ANT_DLY=16436U
antenna_delay.rx_antd_source: Hardcoded #define per role: SS_TWR_INIT_RX_ANT_DLY=16436U, SS_TWR_RESP_RX_ANT_DLY=16436U, SS_TWR_ANCHOR_INIT_RX_ANT_DLY=16436U

values.physical_m: 257.2 ns * c / 2 is NOT correct — this is one-way, so 257.2 ns * 0.2998 m/ns = 77.1 m equivalent path. As antenna delay, the round-trip contribution = 2 * 16436 * ~15.65 ps = 514.4 ns.

antenna_delay.independence_note: TX_ANTD and LDE_RXANTD are FORCED EQUAL to 16436U in every role. dwt_setrxantennadelay() and dwt_settxantennadelay() are separate API calls writing to independent registers (LDE_IF 0x2E:0x1804 vs TX_ANTD 0x18:0x00), but the application hardcodes the same value for both. Per-device calibration is NOT implemented.
antenna_delay.otp_usage: dwt_initialise(DWT_LOADUCODE) does NOT include OTP antenna delay read flags. tag_print_otp_diag() (tag_app.c:265) reads OTP addresses 0x01C/0x01D/0x01E for diagnostic printing only (gated by APP_TAG_OTP_DIAG) — values are NOT used for configuration. OTP antenna delay factory values are completely ignored.
antenna_delay.unicast_comparison: Unicast firmware uses identical values: SS_TWR_INIT_TX_ANT_DLY=16436U, SS_TWR_INIT_RX_ANT_DLY=16436U, SS_TWR_RESP_TX_ANT_DLY=16436U, SS_TWR_RESP_RX_ANT_DLY=16436U (unicast/src/ss_twr_init.c:25-26, unicast/src/ss_twr_resp.c:30-31).

aps011_calls.note: The function exists in the driver (deca_range_tables.c, full APS011 range-bias correction tables for all channels/PRFs). However, ZERO application code calls dwt_getrangebias(). No range-bias correction is applied anywhere in the ranging path. The driver API header (deca_device_api.h:307) even notes that range bias values are 'platform dependent and should therefore be managed at user' level.

findings.description: TX_POWER register (0x1E) is NEVER written by application code. The only write path is dwt_configuretxrf() (deca_device.c:620), which the application never calls. TX_POWER retains POR default (0x0E082848 for Ch5 PRF64).
findings.file_line: drivers/dw1000/src/deca_device.c:620 (driver only), no app call site exists

findings.description: TC_PGDELAY register (0x2B:0x0B) is NEVER written by application code. Three write sites exist in the driver (deca_device.c:617, 3687, 3895) but all are inside driver-internal functions. The application never calls dwt_configuretxrf(). TC_PGDELAY retains POR default 0xC0 for Ch5.

SYS_CFG DIS_STXP bit (bit 18 of 0x04) is NEVER explicitly set or cleared by application code. dwt_setsmarttxpower() exists in the driver (deca_device.c:2228) but is never called. dwt_configure() writes SYS_CFG but only modifies RXM110K and PHR_MODE bits — DIS_STXP is not touched. POR default DIS_STXP=0 means Smart TX Power remains ENABLED.

TX_ANTD and LDE_RXANTD are explicitly written by all three application roles (init, resp, anchor_init) in their configure_radio() functions. All use the same hardcoded value 16436U (0x4034). TX and RX delays are forced equal — no per-device or per-role differentiation.

TX_POWER POR default 0x0E082848 is the DW1000 User Manual recommended value for Ch5 PRF64 in smart power mode. This is acceptable for the application. However, the power level was never explicitly verified or tuned for DWM1001C module — the 0x0E082848 value may not be optimal for the specific module's PA characteristics.
findings.file_line: drivers/dw1000/include/deca_regs.h:534 (TX_POWER_MAN_DEFAULT = 0x0E080222 is the MANUAL default, NOT the smart default)

findings.description: TC_PGDELAY POR default for Ch5 is 0xC0, which matches the DW1000 User Manual recommendation (deca_regs.h:997 TC_PGDELAY_CH5 = 0xC0). Acceptable for this application.

Smart TX Power (DIS_STXP=0) is appropriate. All frames are in the same duration bucket (<0.25ms at 6.8 Mbps with 128 preamble), so smart power introduces zero differential between poll and response. No ranging asymmetry from this source.

Init sequence: uwb_bringup.c → dwt_initialise(DWT_LOADUCODE) → per-role configure_radio() → dwt_configure(). Driver owns: LDO tune, XTAL trim, LDE microcode, channel/PLL/RF config, AGC, baseband tuning. Application owns: antenna delays (hardcoded 16436U), frame filtering, LED enable. NOBODY owns: TX_POWER, TC_PGDELAY, DIS_STXP — all left at POR defaults.

Smart TX Power causes ZERO power differential between tag poll (17B, 174.6µs) and anchor response V3 (36B, 197.0µs). Both fall into BOOSTP250 bucket (< 0.25ms). All four frame types in the system are in this same bucket. Power asymmetry from Smart TX Power is not a ranging error source.
findings.file_line: uwb_ss_twr_shared.h:74,56 (frame lengths), DW1000 User Manual Table 18 (power thresholds)

findings.description: Antenna delays are hardcoded to 16436U for ALL devices — tags and anchors, TX and RX. No per-device calibration. OTP factory-programmed antenna delays (address 0x01C) are read for diagnostic printing only (tag_app.c:271-273, gated by APP_TAG_OTP_DIAG) but NEVER used for configuration. The dwt_initialise() call uses DWT_LOADUCODE (0x01) with no OTP antenna delay flags. This means every DWM1001C module uses the same delay regardless of its individual RF path characteristics. Expected per-device variation: ±1-3 ns (±15-45 cm range error).

TX and RX antenna delays are forced equal (both 16436U). In principle, TX and RX paths through the DWM1001C module antenna have different electrical lengths. For SS-TWR the relevant quantity is (TX_delay_A + RX_delay_B) for the initiator leg and (RX_delay_B + TX_delay_B) for the responder leg. Forcing TX=RX means the sum is always 2*16436 per device regardless of the actual TX/RX asymmetry. This is standard practice (Decawave examples do the same) and is acceptable when the total round-trip delay is calibrated as a single combined value, which 16436U represents.

dwt_getrangebias() (APS011 range-bias correction) exists in the driver (deca_range_tables.c:636) with full correction tables for all channels and PRFs, but is NEVER called by any application code. Range-bias correction compensates for the received-signal-level-dependent ranging error in the DW1000 LDE. At short ranges (<5m) this bias can be 10-20cm. Not applying it means all ranges have an uncorrected RSL-dependent bias.
findings.file_line: drivers/dw1000/src/deca_range_tables.c:636 (defined), zero call sites in SS-TWR/ or apps/
